title: Form 6, voter roll deletions: What Election Commission told the Supreme Court
shows: The Indian Express explains what the Election Commission's affidavit of 26 October 2026 in the Supreme Court means for electors. It sets the affidavit's account of the online Form 6 beside the paper's report of 12 July that a declaration about the last intensive revision had been inserted within the form for every state, and beside the Commission's press note of 26 September. By the paper's account, the Commission decided on 21 October that the online application will be in two parts, so that a new elector can apply through Form 6 without the declaration, which remains a separate requirement where a revision is under way. It also sets out the West Bengal appeals, of which, by the Commission's data, 16.10 lakh were filed against orders of the judicial officers that put names back on the roll, and the affidavit's account of how the Commission takes decisions.
quote: Now, in the counter-affidavit, the EC has admitted that the way the declaration was added to the ECINET portal — on which the electoral rolls sit — was construed as an amendment to the Form 6, even though there was no such amendment.

title: ECI’s stand that additional declaration is not part of Form 6 comes days after SC said it will examine ‘new’ Form 6
shows: Krishnadas Rajagopal reads the Election Commission's affidavit, which says the additional declaration is not part of the statutory Form 6, against the Supreme Court's oral remark of 12 October that the new Form 6 was neither approved nor disapproved in the Bihar judgment and that the Court would examine it. He sets out the petitioners' argument that electors deleted in the revision are made to apply again as fresh voters through Form 6, and the Commission's reply that the declaration let electors give their details in a single document.
quote: “The Declaration is a document provided by SIR orders and is NOT a part of Form 6, which is the statutory Form for inclusion in the electoral roll,” the affidavit said.
